applicable_when: The kernel transposes a (128,128,3,3) tensor with xnumel=9 and ynumel=16384. The current launch uses XBLOCK=128 for xnumel=9, meaning cdiv(9,128)=1 block in X and 2048 blocks in Y, giving grid=(1,2048). With 132 SMs this is barely 0.97 waves. Worse, XBLOCK=128 wastes 119/128 threads per block (93% masked by xmask) since only 9 X-elements exist. The fix is to use @triton.autotune to explore smaller XBLOCK values (e.g., 16, 32) paired with larger YBLOCK values (e.g., 32, 64, 128) so that: (1) fewer threads are wasted on masked X lanes, (2) each CTA does more useful work per launch, and (3) SM utilization improves.
